title: Front panel of a Rigol DM3058 digital multimeter
objects_and_counts: One benchtop digital multimeter device is visible, photographed from the front.
Zero people are visible in the image.

Five circular banana-style input terminals are visible on the right side of the front panel (three red, two black); some are partially cropped by the device bezel but are individually distinguishable.
One rectangular USB-A type port is visible at the left side of the front panel.
One round power button with a green/yellow ring is visible at lower left of the front panel.
One LCD screen/display is visible in the upper-left-to-center area of the front panel showing measurement readouts.

Multiple rectangular and round pushbuttons are visible on the front: two larger orange/yellow buttons at upper right of the display area, a cluster of five grey round/oval directional/auto controls to the right of the display, and three rows of smaller blue/grey rectangular function keys across the lower half of the front panel. All keys are visible and distinct; exact key counts can be read from the image (see visible_text for labels).
Two grey rubber corner bumpers (left and right) are visible protecting the front corners of the instrument.
spatial_relations: The main LCD display occupies the upper-left to center portion of the front panel; numeric readouts are left-aligned inside that display area.
A row of blue/grey rectangular function keys runs below the display across the central lower half of the front panel.

To the right of the display is a circular directional/auto control cluster (up/down/left/right with an Auto center) and above it two yellow/orange rectangular buttons labeled 'Run' 'Hold' and 'Single'.

The five circular input terminals are grouped vertically on the right edge of the front panel with red terminals at the top and bottom and black terminals between them; labels such as HI and LO are adjacent to specific terminals.
The USB-A port is located at the left edge of the front panel, roughly level with the top of the display.
The round power button is at the lower-left corner of the front panel, below the leftmost function keys.
Grey rubber protective bumpers are attached to the four corners (visible at left and right front corners) and wrap slightly around the sides of the instrument.
colours_and_materials: The instrument housing is primarily off-white/light grey plastic on the front panel.
Protective bumpers and side handles appear to be medium grey rubber or plastic with a textured edge.
Front-panel function keys are primarily light blue/grey rectangles; two rectangular buttons to the right of the display are yellow/orange.
Banana-style input terminals are coloured red and black (three red, two black) with surrounding white panel labeling.
The LCD display has a light background with dark text (black digits and labels) and appears backlit.
uncertainties: Some small text and symbols on the lower row of function keys and near individual terminals are partially obscured or too small to read precisely; transcription above includes the most legible labels but may omit microscopic labels.

The very small characters adjacent to some connector symbols (for example exact voltage or polarity icons) are partly unreadable at this resolution and were not transcribed beyond what is clearly legible.
The display line 'M 20V S' and some display fragments may include additional characters that are not fully legible; '095.337mA' is transcribed from visible digits but minor digits could be uncertain.

The device model text '5 1/2 Digits' was transcribed as shown on the panel styling; small punctuation or spacing on that line is read as presented but could differ from the original product typography.
